summary.text: Illapa Sairitupac is a social worker and tenant organizer from Manhattan's Lower East Side and the Democratic nominee for this open seat. He is the son of Peruvian immigrants, holds a Master of Social Work from NYU, and has organized on housing, climate and immigration issues; he previously ran for this seat in 2022. He is running on taxing high earners, expanding affordable and social housing, and opposing ICE enforcement in New York.

paragraphs.text: Describes himself as the son of Peruvian immigrants and has lived on the Lower East Side for almost 14 years, according to his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
Holds a Master of Social Work from NYU and previously worked as a mental healthcare worker.

Describes himself as a local tenant organizer and an organizer with the This Land is Ours Community Land Trust, which advocates for community land trusts in Lower Manhattan; says he has led Know Your Rights trainings and built local networks against ICE.

In his 2022 survey he described himself as a social worker and climate organizer, said he volunteered on the 2021 Tax the Rich campaign, and said he was arrested in 2021 while protesting in support of the Build Public Renewables Act.

Ran for the Democratic nomination for this Assembly seat in 2022, initially considering a State Senate challenge to Brian Kavanagh before shifting to the Assembly race; he was endorsed by NYC-DSA and the Working Families Party and lost the June 28, 2022 primary to Grace Lee, 48.6% to 34.5%.
Served as co-chair of candidate recruitment for NYC-DSA until he resigned that position to run for the Assembly again in 2026, according to City & State.

Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for the open seat with 36.5% of the vote in a six-candidate field, ahead of Jasmin Sanchez (17.6%); Grace Lee, the incumbent, ran for State Senate instead of seeking re-election.
